newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar.

text.p: The shekel weakened against the dollar on Tuesday in dull trading reflecting the firm U.S. currency abroad, dealers said.
Late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.4097 shekels.
"Trading was very quiet today and the shekel weakened against the dollar after the dollar rose against the mark on Monday," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.

"The Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market on a relatively low scale," he said, adding it was buying dollars to prevent a fall in the basket of foreign currencies, against which the shekel is measured, below its trading band.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the currency basket, which has been trading at the bottom its band for three months.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.4100 shekels against 3.4010 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6785 shekels against 3.6778 on Friday.
On Monday the Bank of Israel did not set a representative rate because of the Jewish Passover holiday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded at 2.6918 per 100 yen compared with 2.6981 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9690 compared with 1.9819 on Friday.
